question: Can a useful weak-region start still earn refinement with 1.5 rather than 2.5 seconds remaining after existing clearance/polish reserves? Only the speculative after-recovery weak-region branch changes; early missing-feature scheduling and every acceptance rule remain unchanged.
caseSelection: Jigsaw has a proven skipped-start cliff. Fine-checker and orb are photo error regressions in the last replay. Viking previously regressed when speculative feature work consumed refinement time.
protocol: Fresh processes, grids and original photo crop/mask each run. Four cases x two clock advances x two frozen runtimes. Alternate runtime order by case/delay. Advance global performance.now once at first directFitting, preserving all later deadlines. This is a scheduling counterfactual, not a CPU speedup claim. No saved templates enter fitting.
criteria: Compare independent exported-mask error, selected counts, final paper/geometry checks and actual real elapsed time.
No adoption based on the jigsaw alone. Any lost accepted case or delayed ordinary-fit regression requires investigation.
Keep the production fitter unchanged and preserve failed outcomes. A useful result requires broader corpus and browser QA before integration.
replaySettings: Use runs[0].settings: the original caller inputs. Do not use report.settings, which can include a post-fit increase of materialResolution.

retiredPredecessor.reason: The first runner reused result.report.settings, which includes a post-fit paperVerification upgrade to materialResolution=700, instead of the original runs[0].settings. This changes solver work and cannot replay the original production schedule. Partial outputs remain preserved; do not interpret as the planned benchmark.

decision: Do not integrate the lowered late-feature threshold. It does not lower delayed-jigsaw error, worsens the undelayed fine checkerboard and does not rescue the delayed Viking. More late search is not an established robustness improvement.
diagnosis: At zero delay the fine checkerboard newly performs 0.389 seconds of feature initialization, 0.399 seconds of fine fitting, and an additional clearance comparison. Main curve refinement falls from 2.471 to 1.153 seconds; independent error rises from 1.700% to 2.188%.

At two-second delay neither fine-checker run enters the changed feature branch, yet one fails at 5.404%. This exposes remaining timing/checkpoint sensitivity, not a proven effect of the threshold change. Stage durations containing the artificial clock jump are not CPU timings.
The jigsaw changes from four-by-three to four-by-four at two-second delay, but independent error rises from 1.3025% to 1.3450%. More plausible cut counts alone are not proof of a better result.
